lockup.summary: The company, its directors and officers, and holders of nearly all its stock cannot sell for at least 180 days after the prospectus date. The lead underwriters can allow sales sooner by written consent, and some exceptions apply.

what: It is developing pills that block a protein behind harmful inflammation in heart and brain diseases.
risks: It has a short history, has no drug sales, expects continued losses, and may never make a profit. Its losses raise doubt it can keep operating.
None of its drug candidates is approved. If it cannot sell them or is delayed, its business will be badly hurt.
Unfavorable currency exchange rate changes could raise its costs and make it use up its cash faster.
Its drugs target NLRP3, a new target, so it is hard to predict how long, how costly or how likely success is.
Its business depends heavily on the success of one drug, ruvonoflast.
